Topic: Introduction to Partial Differential Equations (PDEs)

Target audience: University students (Engineering/Physics/Mathematics)

Section: section_1 — Defining the Problem: ODE vs. PDE

Lecture lines:
ODEs track change in one variable, like time.
PDEs model complex phenomena across multiple variables.
Think of a single pendulum versus pond ripples.

Planned animations:
Create two text objects: 'ODE: One Variable' and 'PDE: Many Variables'. Color: #FFFFFF.
Show a vertical line oscillating (pendulum) labeled 'ODE'. Color: #FF9900.
Show a 2D grid ripple (pond) labeled 'PDE'. Color: #00CCFF.

Section: section_2 — Visualizing Multidimensional Change

Lecture lines:
Partial derivatives measure change along specific axes.
Imagine a terrain; slope varies in x and y.
Heat maps visualize these gradients on surfaces.

Planned animations:
Display a 3D terrain surface labeled 'Temperature Field'. Color: #FF4444.
Show a slice along the X-axis keeping Y constant; highlight the slope. Color: #FFFF00.
Show a slice along the Y-axis keeping X constant; highlight the slope. Color: #00FF00.

Section: section_3 — The Core Equation: The Heat Equation

Lecture lines:
The heat equation links diffusion to spatial curvature.
Rate of temperature change equals the diffusion rate.
Visualize heat spreading from a warm radiator.
[Asset: cat_on_radiator_diffusing]
Curvature drives the flow of heat over time.

Planned animations:
Display the Heat Equation text: 'u_t = alpha * u_xx'. Color: #FFFFFF.
Show a heat source (radiator) and a temperature gradient through a block. Color: #FF4500.
Highlight the diffusion term 'u_xx' by flashing it while the temperature flattens over time. Color: #00FF00.

Section: section_4 — Boundary and Initial Conditions

Lecture lines:
PDEs require context to solve uniquely.
Initial conditions define the starting state.
Boundary conditions constrain the edges of space.

Planned animations:
Show an empty line labeled 'Initial State (t=0)'. Color: #FFFFFF.
Animate the line forming a plucked 'V' shape. Color: #FF00FF.
Add two solid vertical bars at the ends labeled 'Fixed Boundaries'. Color: #FFFF00.

Section: section_5 — Applications and Wrap-up

Lecture lines:
PDEs are the fundamental language of nature.
They govern fluids, electromagnetism, and quantum fields.
[Asset: drone_turbulence_simulation]
Real-time solvers handle complex environmental turbulence.
PDEs unlock mastery over physical reality.

Planned animations:
Display text: 'PDEs: Nature's Language'. Color: #FFFFFF.
Pop up icons for 'Fluid' (droplet), 'Electromagnetism' (wave), and 'Quantum' (atom). Color: #00FFFF.
Show a drone silhouette flying smoothly as turbulence vectors stabilize. Color: #FFFFFF.

        return mobject
